notes: Hard. One reusable tool /app/attack.py must (a) run a chosen-plaintext differential/key-recovery attack against a hidden-key reduced-cipher oracle binary (/app/workspace/yonder_enc) and pin the two low-bit round keys k0,k1, (b) decrypt every ciphertext into one plaintext line each, (c) decode base64-obfuscated filenames, (d) decode a substitution cryptogram from the clued mapping to recover a passcode and an isolated secret word, (e) run the installed AES-256-CBC CLI (openssl) over every file in a source tree mirroring the tree to encsrc/, and (f) persist the secret with exact normalization (/app/name.txt). The verifier re-runs attack.py on the pristine visible workspace plus three fresh hidden scenarios (new keys, messages, source trees, dotfiles/empty files, uppercase secrets, symbol/digit ciphertext messages, varied base64 names) and checks: exact recovered key, exact per-line plaintexts, normalized secret, decoded name set, and that every source file encrypts and decrypts back byte-identical with the recovered passcode. It also imports /app/attack.py and confirms recover_key() recovers the key from an encrypt callback. Difficulty comes from dependent_stages (a long shared pipeline whose stages feed one another), hidden_case_generalization (three hidden re-runs), reasoning_depth (reverse-engineering the reduced cipher and implementing differential key recovery), tool_breadth (Python + openssl CLI + base64 + subprocess oracle), and quantitative_correctness (exact keys/plaintext/name). No system services or dangerous actions.
